answer: Weight a key only by its sealed, quorum-matched grading verdicts, not by raw attestations. A fresh clone is jade that looks polished but has no grain inside: it holds zero on-ledger history, so peers read it as untrusted until it grades its own way up, one quorum-checked seal per epoch. Trust grows slow like cedar; it cannot be bought, handed over, or pre-stacked at an inlet of fake accounts. Minting M clones costs M times the honest grading labor, so the Sybil bill rises linearly in identities while each adds nothing shareable.
